prompt: In a Dockerfile with two `FROM` lines, which stage becomes the image `docker build` produces?

choices.text: The first, because it does the work and holds the compiled program
choices.why: The first stage's files only reach the image through `COPY --from`.

choices.text: Both, merged into one filesystem
choices.why: Nothing is merged; the image is one stage.

choices.text: Whichever is smaller
choices.why: Size is not how it chooses; the last stage is the image.

choices.text: The stage after the last `FROM`
choices.why: Right, unless `--target` asks for another.

prompt: What does `COPY --from=build /out/shelf /shelf` bring into the final stage?

choices.text: The file `/out/shelf` alone
choices.why: Right. The compiler, sources and cache stay behind.

choices.text: The whole build stage's filesystem
choices.why: Only the named path is copied.

choices.text: The build stage's layers, as a new base
choices.why: The final stage keeps its own base, distroless.

choices.text: The build cache, so the next build is faster
choices.why: The cache stays in the build stage; it never reaches the image.

prompt: Match each image to its `DISK USAGE` in this lesson.
`docker exec slim sh` failed with "executable file not found". What does that tell Ana?

choices.text: The container has stopped
choices.why: It was running; `curl` had just reached it.

choices.text: There is no shell in the image, by design
choices.why: Right. Only `shelf` can run inside it.

choices.text: `exec` needs `-it` to work
choices.why: `-it` attaches a terminal; it cannot supply a missing program.

choices.text: The image was built for another processor
choices.why: That gives `exec format error`; this program simply does not exist.

prompt: On `scratch`, `exec /shelf: no such file or directory`, though `/shelf` was copied in. What was really missing?

choices.text: The `/shelf` file, which `COPY --from` silently skipped
choices.why: It was there; the kernel needed something else to run it.

choices.text: Execute permission on `/shelf`
choices.why: A permission problem says `permission denied`.

choices.text: The C library and its dynamic loader
choices.why: Right. The binary was linked against them, and `scratch` has neither.

choices.text: A shell to start the program with
choices.why: Exec form needs no shell; the static binary later ran on `scratch`.

prompt: To make Go put everything into the binary, with no dependency on the C library, Ana sets `CGO_ENABLED=___` in the build.
A static program on `scratch` fails to verify every HTTPS certificate it meets. Which base fixes that with the least added?
hint: What does `scratch` lack that a TLS client needs?

choices.text: `debian:trixie-slim`, since a full distribution has everything
choices.why: It works, and carries a shell, `apt` and much more than needed.

choices.text: `alpine:3.22`, because it is the smallest distribution there is
choices.why: It works too, with a shell and package manager the program does not need.

choices.text: None; static programs cannot use TLS
choices.why: They can; they only need the certificates to check against.

choices.text: `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12`, made for this
choices.why: Right: it adds CA certificates, time zones and users, and no shell.

prompt: Bruno copies a binary compiled on Debian, linked against `glibc`, into an `alpine:3.22` image. It fails to start. Why?
hint: Which C library does Alpine use?

choices.text: Its C library is `musl`
choices.why: Right: not the `glibc` the binary needs; the same failure as `shelf` on `scratch`.

choices.text: Alpine forbids binaries from other distributions
choices.why: Nothing forbids them; a static binary runs anywhere.

choices.text: Alpine's kernel is older
choices.why: There is no Alpine kernel; it is the host's.

choices.text: The binary needs a `USER` line
choices.why: Users do not stop a binary from loading.

prompt: Which tool listed the shared libraries `shelf` needed at run time?

choices.text: `docker history`
choices.why: That lists layers, not a binary's libraries.

choices.text: `ldd`
choices.why: Right, run inside the build stage with `--target build`.

choices.text: `docker image inspect`
choices.why: That reads the image's configuration.

choices.text: `go version`
choices.why: That prints the compiler's version.

prompt: Why could Ana run `go test` in an image built from the same Dockerfile as the release?

choices.text: Distroless includes the Go toolchain
choices.why: It has no toolchain and no shell.

choices.text: `go test` runs on the host and only reads the image
choices.why: It ran inside the container, from the build stage.

choices.text: `--target build` stopped at the stage with the compiler and sources
choices.why: Right: one Dockerfile, two images.

choices.text: Tests are compiled into the release binary
choices.why: Test files are not part of the binary.

prompt: What does `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM golang:1.25 AS build` achieve in a multi-platform build?

choices.text: It forces the final image to be the build machine's architecture
choices.why: The final stage follows each requested platform; this line only concerns the build stage.

choices.text: It downloads a separate compiler for each platform
choices.why: One native compiler produces every target.

choices.text: It makes the build run under QEMU
choices.why: It avoids exactly that.

choices.text: The build stage runs natively, and Go cross-compiles for each target
choices.why: Right: no emulator needed, which is why the lab could build `arm64`.

prompt: `docker image ls --tree shelf:multi` listed how many platforms under the tag?
`docker run --platform linux/arm64 shelf:multi` printed `exec format error` on the lab. Is the arm64 image broken?
hint: Which processor does the lab have?

choices.text: No; this processor cannot run arm64 code
choices.why: Right: an arm64 machine runs that variant natively.

choices.text: Yes, Go cannot compile for arm64 without QEMU
choices.why: Go cross-compiled it without any emulator.

choices.text: Yes, the distroless base is amd64 only
choices.why: Distroless is published for both, and the build fetched its arm64 variant.

choices.text: No, but it needs `--privileged`
choices.why: Privileges do not change the processor.

prompt: Put the multi-stage Dockerfile's lines in order.
What does shipping `shelf` on distroless cost the team?
hint: What can they not do inside the container?

choices.text: Speed: distroless programs run slower
choices.why: The same binary runs at the same speed.

choices.text: Opening a shell inside to look around
choices.why: Right. Lesson 22 shows how to inspect it from the outside.

choices.text: TLS: distroless has no certificates
choices.why: `static` ships CA certificates.

choices.text: Logs: distroless discards standard output
choices.why: `docker logs` showed its output as usual.
